 This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 14.3.2016 Passed In Mvc
No.1194/2015 On The File Of 22Nd Additional Small
Causes Judge, 20Th Acmm, Member, Mact, Bengaluru,
Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation
And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner apart from seeking enhancement of compensation questioned the
attribution of 25% of contributory negligence against him as per order dated 14.03.2016 in Mvc
No.1194/2015 by the Xxii Additional Small Causes Judge and Xx Additional Chief Metropolitan
Magistrate and Mact, Bengaluru (Scch-24) ('the Tribunal' for short).
2.  For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are, on 29.12.2014 at 9.00 p.m., while the petitioner was ridding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-E-5104 as pillion rider, near Indian Petrol Bunk, Paramaradoddi,
Bannerghatta, Bengaluru, a car bearing NC: 2024:KHC:32635 No.KA-03-MP-7389 driven from the opposite direction dashed against the motor cycle, due to which the rider and two pillion riders including the petitioner sustained the injuries.
The petitioner took treatment at Vijayashree hospital and approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
The Claim was opposed by the respondents.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal, by impugned judgment assessed compensation of Rs.50,676/- and attributed 25% of contributory negligence against the petitioner and awarded 75% of the compensation.
Questioning the same the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Gurudeva Prasad K.T, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri. Mohan Kumar.T, learned counsel for respondent No.1 and Sri.R.Krishna Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered fracture of middle 1/3rd of right limb.

The evidence of PW4-Dr.S.Ramachandra, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, is placed before the Tribunal explaining the limb disability of 40% and whole body NC: 2024:KHC:32635 disability at 20% on account of non-union of the fractured bone.
The Tribunal did not consider the loss of future income and compensation assessed under different heads is on the lower side and sought for enhancement.
It is further contended that, the petitioner is the pillion rider, there is no question of contributory negligence on which the Tribunal erroneously attributed contributory negligence against him.

sentences.text: Per contra learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that there were three riders on the motor cycle, the accident took place at 9.00 p.m. on the Bannerghatta road, Bengaluru.
At the place of the accident, the width of the road is 18 feet and in spite of it, for the reason of triple riding the rider could not control the motor cycle and hit against the car.
Hence, the attribution of contributory negligence is established on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
The petitioner being one of the pillion rider, who is not expected to ride the bike having two pillion riders.

Hence,
attribution of contributory negligence at 25% by the Tribunal is proper.

To support his contention,
has relied on the judgment of Division Bench of Madras High Court in the case of MANAGING DIRECTOR, TAMIL NADU STATE NC: 2024:KHC:32635 TRANSPORTATION CORPORATION LIMITED VS. ABDUL SALAM AND OTHERS reported in 2004 ACJ 1827.
7.

entities.text: MANAGING DIRECTOR, TAMIL NADU STATE NC: 2024:KHC:32635 TRANSPORTATION CORPORATION LIMITED VS. ABDUL SALAM AND OTHERS reported in 2004 ACJ 1827
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended that there is no medical evidence to show that there was a fracture.
The charge sheet clearly indicate that the petitioner has not suffered disability only simple injuries.
PW4-Doctor is not a treated Doctor and he is professionally engaged in giving false opinion in a case of his nature.
The Tribunal has rightly discarded his opinion evidence.

8. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has contended that the Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation proportionate to the injuries, attributed contributory negligence and it not a case for enhancement or removal of contributory negligence against the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
9. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for both parties and perused the records.
10. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injuries sustained by all the three riders of the motor cycle.
Involvement of car is also not in dispute.

The claim made NC:
2024:KHC:32635 by the rider of the motor cycle by name Sri.Ramachandra @ Ramakrishna.N, was settled before the Lok Adalat in MFA.No.6277/2016 dated 25.06.2019 and insurance company has satisfied the award.
Even in that case also, it is submitted that the contributory negligence of 25%
was taken into account while assessing the compensation.

11. Adverting to the argument of Sri. Gurudeva Prasad K.T, learned counsel for the petitioner that no contributory negligence can be attributed against the pillion rider and no evidence is on record to show that the reason of triple riding was the cause for the accident, on perusal of mahazar it is pertinent to note that, width of the road was 18 feet tar road, 3 feet mud road on either side of the tar road.
Mahazar did not point out where exactly the accident took place.
The IMV report point out that the damage to the motor cycle as well as the car was on the right side of the body.

It is thus,
clear that it was not a head on collision both vehicles rubbed side by side.

12. The Madras High Court in Abdul Salam's case (supra) at para No.12 held that "when three persons travel on motor cycle which is meant for two persons, this courts is of NC: 2024:KHC:32635 the view, the conduct of persons who travel in such a manner is liable for contributory negligence;
especially when their action is contrary to the statute."
50% contributory negligence was attributed on the part of the victim, who was the rider of the motor cycle.

The contributory negligence Mr. Manikanta @ Mani N vs The United India Insurance Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60863367/
3 attributed by the Tribunal has been taken consideration in the Lok Adalat settlement in case of Sri.Ramachandra @ Ramakrishna.S, the rider.

entities.text: Manikanta @ Mani N vs The United India Insurance Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no force in the submission made on behalf of the petitioner.

13. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that there is no evidence on the record that the triple riding was cause of accident, the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kumari Kiran through her father Harinarayan Vs. Sajjan Singh and Others reported in (2015) 1 SCC 539 will not comes to the aid of the petitioner.

entities.text: Harinarayan Vs. Sajjan Singh and Others reported in (2015) 1 SCC 539
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case, it was discussed that contributory negligence cannot be attributed against rider.
When the accident was head on collision and two pillion riders were minors.
Here, in this case, the accident took place at 9.00 p.m., the mahazar did not point out where exactly the accident took place.
The rider of the motor cycle did not dispute 25% of the contributory negligence on his part and NC: 2024:KHC:32635 settle his claim before Lok Adalat.
The rider and the owner of the motor cycle are not a party to this case.
Considering the damage to right side of both vehicles was due to over loading of motor cycle, the rider unable to control the vehicle and hit on the right side body of the car.
So triple riding also contributed for the accident.
Under such circumstances, contributory negligence attributed against the petitioner as pillion rider has to be retained.
Pillion rider cannot claim compensation as bonaza, being the part of triple riding.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled to 75% of compensation only.

14. As regards assessment of compensation is concerned, the petitioner though claims through PW4-doctor, but medical certificate, speaks that the petitioner though has suffered grevious injuries, there is no mention of fractures but he was hospitalized for a week.
The evidence of PW4 is not inspiring the confidence of the Court.
Hence, pain and suffering assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.20,000/- is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.

Tribunal awarded Rs.2,676/- towards medical expenses,
tribunal has assessed Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges, it is maintained.
The petitioner was laid up for three months, hence NC: 2024:KHC:32635 loss of three months income Rs.25,500/- (Rs.8,500/- x 3).
Towards loss of amenities, Tribunal has assessed Rs.10,000/- which is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
These are no grounds to assesses compensation under other heads.

Total compensation comes to Rs.93,176/- as against Rs.50,676/-
assessed by the Tribunal.
The petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.42,500/-.
Out of which 75% works out to Rs.31,875/-.
It is the just compensation the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
